svg.title: Amex Financial Review Survival Gates
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-05-amex-review-gates; chapter number: 5; title: Amex Financial Review Survival Gates; subtitle: Spend curve, payment-app hygiene, spending-power checks and the 14-day window; chart type: decision_tree; nodes: gate: G1; question: Is spend ramping on a curve, 5K then 10K then 15K across months?; pass next: G2; fail action: Slow the ramp and call ahead before any massive purchase; high-velocity spending sat behind 65% of reviewed cases (Colin Matthew, Cal Barton).; gate: G2; question: Are PayPal, Cash App, Square and Venmo transfers kept off the Amex?; pass next: G3; fail action: Move family money to Amex Send and Split instead (Cal Barton).; gate: G3; question: Is check spending power used sparingly, never more than three times a day?; pass next: G4; fail action: Reserve it for purchases above the six-month average spend (CardRight, Cal Barton).; gate: G4; question: If a review letter lands, are the requested documents sent within 14 days?; pass next: Accounts likely retained; 25 of 28 reported decisions kept some accounts; fail action: Call the number on the back of the card the same day and transfer out points you plan to use before the decision lands (Colin Matthew, AskSebby).; caption: Reviews freeze every personal and business card plus Membership Rewards until income is documented; send exactly what is asked, even if the numbers are off.; assumptions note: Case counts come from Cal Barton's samples of 20 and 40 cases; 12 of the 25 retained cases still reported lower limits, fixed limits or closed cards.; note: Sources - Cal Barton, Colin Matthew, CardRight, RJ Financial, AskSebby.

rect.title: gate: G1; question: Is spend ramping on a curve, 5K then 10K then 15K across months?; pass next: G2; fail action: Slow the ramp and call ahead before any massive purchase; high-velocity spending sat behind 65% of reviewed cases (Colin Matthew, Cal Barton).
gate: G2; question: Are PayPal, Cash App, Square and Venmo transfers kept off the Amex?; pass next: G3; fail action: Move family money to Amex Send and Split instead (Cal Barton).

gate: G3; question: Is check spending power used sparingly, never more than three times a day?; pass next: G4; fail action: Reserve it for purchases above the six-month average spend (CardRight, Cal Barton).

gate: G4; question: If a review letter lands, are the requested documents sent within 14 days?; pass next: Accounts likely retained; 25 of 28 reported decisions kept some accounts; fail action: Call the number on the back of the card the same day and transfer out points you plan to use before the decision lands (Colin Matthew, AskSebby).

text.title: Assumptions: Case counts come from Cal Barton's samples of 20 and 40 cases; 12 of the 25 retained cases still reported lower limits, fixed limits or closed cards.
